arxiv-2011-10021.title: Bershadsky-Polyakov vertex algebras at positive integer levels and duality
arxiv-2011-10021.creator: Dražen Adamović, Ana Kontrec
arxiv-2011-10021.description: Abstract . We study the simple Bershadsky-Polyakov algebra 𝒲 k = 𝒲 k ​ ( s ​ l 3 , f θ ) \mathcal{W}_{k}=\mathcal{W}_{k}(sl_{3},f_{\theta}) at positive integer levels and classify their irreducible modules. In this way we confirm the conjecture from [ 9 ] . Next, we study the case k = 1 k=1 .

arxiv-2201-07305.title: Proportional Ranking in Primary Elections: A Case Study
arxiv-2201-07305.creator: Ariel Rosenfeld, Ehud Shapiro, Nimrod Talmon
arxiv-2201-07305.description: Abstract Many democratic political parties hold primary elections, which nicely reflects their democratic nature and promote, among other things, the democratic value of inclusiveness. However, the methods currently used for holding such primary elections may not be the most suitable, especially if some form of proportional ranking is desired.

arxiv-2212-10943.title: DeepGlow: an efficient neural-network emulator of physical afterglow models for gamma-ray bursts and gravitational-wave events
arxiv-2212-10943.creator: Oliver M. Boersma, Joeri van Leeuwen
arxiv-2212-10943.description: Abstract Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and double neutron-star merger gravitational wave events are followed by afterglows that shine from X-rays to radio, and these broadband transients are generally interpreted using analytical models. Such models are relatively fast to execute, and thus easily allow estimates of the energy and geometry parameters of the blast wave, through many trial-and-error model calculations.

arxiv-2307-09018.title: Multimodal LLMs for health grounded in individual-specific data
arxiv-2307-09018.creator: Anastasiya Belyaeva, Justin Cosentino ∗, Farhad Hormozdiari, Krish Eswaran, Shravya Shetty, Greg Corrado, Andrew Carroll, Cory Y. McLean, Nicholas A. Furlotte †
arxiv-2307-09018.description: Abstract Foundation large language models (LLMs) have shown an impressive ability to solve tasks across a wide range of fields including health. To effectively solve personalized health tasks, LLMs need the ability to ingest a diversity of data modalities that are relevant to an individual’s health status.

arxiv-2405-10039.title: High-Scale SUSY from Sgoldstino Inflation
arxiv-2405-10039.description: Abstract We review a number of unimodular no-scale supergravity models with F-term SUSY breaking which support technically natural de Sitter vacua. A variant of these models develops a stage of inflection-point inflation which can be realized for subplanckian field values consistently with the observational data.

arxiv-2502-11760.title: An Edge Labeling of Graphs from Rado’s Partition Regularity Condition
arxiv-2502-11760.creator: Arun J Manattu, Aparna Lakshmanan S
arxiv-2502-11760.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arun J Manattu, Aparna Lakshmanan S. A vertex v v is called an AR-vertex, if v v has distinct edge weight sums for each distinct subset of edges incident on v v . i.e., if { x 1 , x 2 , … , x k } \{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{k}\} are the edge labels of the edges incident on v v , then the 2 k 2^{k} subset sums are all distinct.

arxiv-2507-12070.title: Emergence of Quantised Representations Isolated to Anisotropic Functions
arxiv-2507-12070.creator: George Bird
arxiv-2507-12070.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel methodology for determining representational alignment, which builds upon the existing Spotlight Resonance method. Particularly, this new tool is used to gain insight into how discrete representations can emerge and organise in autoencoder models, through a controlled ablation study in which only the activation function is altered.

arxiv-2508-13016.creator: Jacek Marchwicki, Błażej Żmija
arxiv-2508-13016.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jacek Marchwicki, Błażej Żmija. Let 𝐱 \mathbf{x} be a (non-empty) sequence of positive real numbers. Its achievement set 𝐱 \mathcal{\mathbf{x}} is the set of all the possible sums of the elements of 𝐱 \mathbf{x} .

arxiv-2509-09043.title: Stated Preference for Interaction and Continued Engagement (SPICE): Evaluating an LLM’s Willingness to Re-engage in Conversation
arxiv-2509-09043.creator: Thomas Rost, Martina Figlia, Bernd Wallraff
arxiv-2509-09043.description: Abstract We introduce and evaluate Stated Preference for Interaction and Continued Engagement (SPICE), a simple diagnostic signal elicited by asking a Large Language Model a YES/NO question about its willingness to re-engage with a user’s behavior after reviewing a short transcript.

arxiv-2511-04638.title: Addressing divergent representations from causal interventions on neural networks
arxiv-2511-04638.creator: Satchel Grant, Simon Jerome Han, Alexa R. Tartaglini, Christopher Potts
arxiv-2511-04638.description: Abstract A common approach to mechanistic interpretability is to causally manipulate model representations via targeted interventions in order to understand what those representations encode. Here we ask whether such interventions create out-of-distribution (divergent) representations, and whether this raises concerns about how faithful their resulting explanations are to the target model in its natural state.

arxiv-2512-00981.title: Decomposition of the total wave aberration in generalized optical systems
arxiv-2512-00981.creator: Mateusz Oleszko, Ralf Hambach, Herbert Gross
arxiv-2512-00981.description: Abstract The increasing use of freeform optical surfaces raises the demand for optical design tools developed for generalized systems. In the design process surface-by-surface aberration contributions are of special interest. The expansion of the wave aberration function into field and pupil dependent coefficients is an analytical method used for that purpose.

arxiv-2512-02433.title: Study of fully coupled 3D envelope instability using automatic differentiation
arxiv-2512-02433.creator: Ji Qiang
arxiv-2512-02433.description: Abstract Auto-differentiation is a powerful tool for computing derivatives of simulation results with respect to given parameters. In this letter, we have applied this tool to investigate the instability of a dynamics system that is governed by 21 21 ordinary differential equations.

arxiv-2601-13528.title: Eliciting Harmful Capabilities by Fine-Tuning on Safeguarded Outputs
arxiv-2601-13528.creator: Jackson KaunismaaMATSAvery GriffinAnthropicJohn HughesAnthropicChristina Q KnightScale AI, Mrinank SharmaAnthropic, Erik JonesAnthropic
arxiv-2601-13528.description: Abstract Model developers implement safeguards in frontier models to prevent misuse, for example, by employing classifiers to filter dangerous outputs. In this work, we demonstrate that even robustly safeguarded models can be used to elicit harmful capabilities in open-source models through elicitation attacks .

arxiv-2601-23255.title: Now You Hear Me: Audio Narrative Attacks Against Large Audio–Language Models
arxiv-2601-23255.creator: Ye Yu, Haibo Jin, Yaoning Yu, Jun Zhuang, Haohan Wang
arxiv-2601-23255.description: Abstract Large audio-language models increasingly operate on raw speech inputs, enabling more seamless integration across domains such as voice assistants, education, and clinical triage. This transition, however, introduces a distinct class of vulnerabilities that remain largely uncharacterized. We examine the security implications of this modality shift by designing a text-to-audio jailbreak that embeds disallowed directives within a narrative-style audio stream.

pmc-10595333.title: Promoting healthy learning: A participatory health promotion project with healthcare students
pmc-10595333.creator: T Schloemer, L Domenik, A-C Dreyer, L Scheu
pmc-10595333.description: BackgroundHealth promotion is of great importance during education to prepare future health professionals for their work. Students need to cope with long periods of sitting, stress and high workload through practical training in the healthcare sector. Based on students’ experiences, we developed a project to promote healthy learning at a University of applied Sciences for Health in Germany.

pmc-10597281.title: 3.O. Workshop: Students avoiding school toilets: a universal, unrecognized & rarely discussed public health issue
pmc-10597281.creator: Organised by: EHESP School of Public Health (France), EUPHA-CAPH, Chair persons: Emmanuelle Godeau (France), Julia Dratva (EUPHA-CAPH)
pmc-10597281.description: Based on recent statistics, access to school toilets can be considered no more an issue in the European region (UNICEF, 2020). However, presence is not equivalent to use. Four complementary perspectives will illustrate this universal yet unrecognised and underdiscussed public health issue: the avoidance of school toilets by children and adolescents.

pmc-11453355.title: 7770 Damage of Ovarian Vasculature by Chemotherapies induces Ovarian Dysfunction in Mice
pmc-11453355.creator: W So, R Dong, Y Luan, A Abazarikia, S Y Kim
pmc-11453355.description: Disclosure: W. So: None. R. Dong: None. Y. Luan: None. A. Abazarikia: None. S. Kim: None. Background: Chemotherapy demonstrates efficacy to destroying cancer cells; however, it can inadvertently impact normal healthy cells, leading to irreversible side effects, particularly affecting the ovaries in female patients.

pmc-11638686.title: Gamified Digital Mental Health Interventions for Young People: Scoping Review of Ethical Aspects During Development and Implementation
pmc-11638686.creator: Wanda Spahl, Valeria Motta, Kate Woodcock, Giovanni Rubeis, Tiffany Leung, Kai Erenli, Robert Ranisch, Menna Brown
pmc-11638686.description: BackgroundYoung people are particularly at risk of developing mental health problems, a challenge exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Digital tools such as apps and chatbots show promise in providing accessible, cost-effective, and less stigmatized ways of strengthening their mental health.

pmc-11667291.title: Balancing the Functionality and Biocompatibility of Materials with a Deep-Learning-Based Inverse Design Framework
pmc-11667291.creator: Xiaofang Li, Hanle Chen, Jiachen Yan, Guohong Liu, Chengjun Li, Xiaoxia Zhou, Yan Wang, Yinbao Wu, Bing Yan, Xiliang Yan
pmc-11667291.description: The rational design of molecules with the desired functionality presents a significant challenge in chemistry. Moreover, it is worth noting that making chemicals safe and sustainable is crucial to bringing them to the market. To address this, we propose a novel deep learning framework developed explicitly for inverse design of molecules with both functionality and biocompatibility.

pmc-11691786.title: VIRTUAL REALITY IN RESPITE: USING IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE TO ASSESS ADOPTION OF VR WITH PLWD
pmc-11691786.creator: Mary Milnamow, Lillian Agyemang, Louanne Bakk, Jason Dauenhauer
pmc-11691786.description: In the U.S., 6.7 million older adults are living with dementia (PLwD); this number is estimated to double by 2040. Community-based volunteer respite programs are vital for PLwD to receive social connections and engagement. Virtual Reality (VR) programming for PLwD is typically used in nursing homes, residential care, and rehabilitation settings.

pmc-12387987.title: Re-Evaluating the Contraction Stress Test for Term Fetal Growth Restriction Fetuses: A Retrospective Study †
pmc-12387987.creator: Roie Alter, Hagar Herz, Adiel Cohen, Naama Lessans, Yossef Ezra, Doron Kabiri, Erich Cosmi
pmc-12387987.description: Background: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality, yet optimal intrapartum management remains debated. The contraction stress test (CST) has been proposed as a tool to assess fetal tolerance to labor, but its prognostic value in FGR pregnancies is unclear.

pmc-12831947.title: Allergic Reactions to Brimonidine 0.15%: A Case Series
pmc-12831947.creator: Fatin Nabila Mat Nawi, Mae-Lynn C Bastion
pmc-12831947.description: Topical brimonidine is an effective anti-glaucoma agent and is usually well tolerated. This retrospective case series aimed to demonstrate the clinical features of brimonidine 0.15% (Alphagan P; Irvine, CA: Allergan Inc.) allergy. Five cases were found from one ophthalmologist’s two-year patient records. Patients’ ages ranged from 54 to 80 years.

pmc-12880064.title: Long-term association between water intake and kidney function in a population at high cardiovascular risk
pmc-12880064.creator: Indira Paz-Graniel, Cristina Valle-Hita, Nancy Babio, Lluís Serra-Majem, Jesus Vioque, María Dolores Zomeño, Dolores Corella, Xavier Pintó, Naomi Cano-Ibáñez, Josep A. Tur, Esther Cuadrado-Soto, J.A. Martínez, Andrés Díaz-López, Laura Torres-Collado, Albert Goday, Rebeca Fernández-Carrión, Mariela N
pmc-12880064.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Highlights•Water intake might prevent kidney function decline.•Plain water might preserve kidney function in individuals at high cardiovascular risk.•Tap water rather than bottled water might be beneficial for kidney health. Introduction

Kidney function decline is a common ageing condition, which could be exacerbated by comorbidities such as obesity, diabetes and/or hypertension, and that could lead to the onset of chronic kidney disease (CKD) [1].

pmc-13231694.title: TFRC promotes ferroptosis to suppress breast cancer bone metastasis via the activation of HIF-1 pathway
pmc-13231694.creator: Lulin Liu, Yan Gao, Dongmin Yu, Deping Li, Sheng Liu, Chunlei He, Chunlin Xiao, Yongjun Ye, Kai Zhao, Fangtian Xu, Yanming Hao
pmc-13231694.description: BackgroundBreast cancer with bone metastasis remains a significant clinical challenge. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death process, may influence metastasis. However, the role of key regulators like transferrin receptor (TFRC) is unclear.MethodsTranscriptome sequencing identified ferroptosis-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in tibial tumors from a breast cancer mouse model with bone metastasis versus breast cancer cells.

pmc-13317464.title: Accuracy of Digital Impressions of Implants With Angulated and Different Vertical Positions in the Full Arch: An In Vitro Study
pmc-13317464.creator: Sina Safari, Neshat Atashpareh, Hamed Bahrami Maleki
pmc-13317464.description: PurposeThe present in vitro study was conducted to evaluate the trueness and precision of full‐arch digital impressions of implants with different angulations and vertical positions.MethodsTwo angulated and two parallel fixtures were placed on two typodonts (subcrestal and crestal). Four scan bodies were fixed on the fixtures. Typodonts were scanned using 3Shape TRIOS 3 and Planmeca Emerald scanners.

pmc-13374351.title: Autoimmune diseases and risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes: a population-based cohort study of five million pregnancies in the UK
pmc-13374351.creator: Megha Singh, Anuradhaa Subramanian, Steven Wambua, Neil Cockburn, Stephanie J Hanley, Siang Ing Lee, Arturo Gonzalez-Izquierdo, Mairead Black, John A Reynolds, Francesca L Crowe, Krishnarajah Nirantharakumar
pmc-13374351.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background With an increasing trend in the prevalence of maternal autoimmune diseases in pregnancy, there is need for evidence on the association between autoimmune diseases and pregnancy outcomes.MethodsThis population-based cohort study used data on pregnancies from primary care practices that contributed to the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) database (Gold and Aurum) between 2000 and 2022, linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES).

pmc-13505861.title: Arc of Buhler pseudoaneurysm complicated by an arterioportal fistula: a combined endovascular and open surgical approach
pmc-13505861.creator: Islam Elhelf, Kate Elmore, Shaan Haider, Sarah Hanna, Abul Rahman Abualruz, Lane Estes, Steven Colquhoun
pmc-13505861.description: The Arc of Buhler (AoB) is a rare anatomic variant characterized by direct anastomosis between the celiac artery and the superior mesenteric artery. There is a relative paucity of data regarding this anatomy, likely due to its rather low incidence.

pmc-13589065.title: Structural optimization and freeze-thaw stabilization of carnauba wax and beta-sitosterol bigels via peanut protein and sodium alginate complexation
pmc-13589065.creator: Chun Hu, Chunyu Li, Weinong Zhang, Junbo He, Yanpeng Zhang, Lijuan Han
pmc-13589065.description: This study investigated the influence of peanut protein/sodium alginate (PP/SA) complex and oleogel-to-hydrogel ratio on the structure, mechanical properties and stability of carnauba wax/β-sitosterol-based bigels. The results indicated adding SA increased PP mean particle size from 88.1 to 395.2 and 729.6 nm, and absolute zeta-potential from 38.5 to 53.0 and 60.5 mV, and improved its surface hydrophobicity.
